t: You're looking at a terrace of nineteenth-century houses with iron railings, numbers twenty-two to forty-six on Albert Street in Camden Town. The street takes its name from Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, the husband of Queen Victoria. He was consort from their marriage on the tenth of February 1840 until his death in 1861, and Victoria gave him the title Prince Consort in 1857. So the name here is a tribute to the royal husband of the age in which these houses were built.
